name: Aqara Smart Lock U300 (US)

radios.note: CSA lists Thread and Bluetooth. Aqara's spec sheet also lists NFC for cards and phones.

matter.note: CSA lists the Smart Lock U300 from Lumi United (Aqara): Matter 1.2, certified 2024-06-04, product ID 0x2801. The listing does not name a region.

apple_home.note: Needs an Apple home hub (HomePod mini, HomePod 2nd gen or Apple TV 4K) for Thread, remote control and Siri. Apple Home Key is listed as an unlock method.

google_home.note: Needs a Thread border router that supports Matter.

alexa.note: Needs a Thread border router that supports Matter.

smartthings.note: Needs a Thread border router that supports Matter.

home_assistant.note: Aqara's pages seen name Apple Home, Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings; none we saw names Home Assistant. The Matter integration may work, unconfirmed.

hubRequired.note: Aqara disagrees with itself: the retail spec table says a hub is required, while the FAQ says basic lock functions work without one and an M3, M100 or G5 Pro is recommended for remote control and automations.

localControl.note: No Aqara source states local-only control.

lockFit.note: Aqara's first lever lock; replaces the door handle with a built-in lock for indoor and outdoor use.

keypad.note: PIN keypad on the lock, alongside a fingerprint reader. Fingerprint capacity is listed as 50 on the spec sheet and 25 in the FAQ.

power.note: Four AA batteries, up to 10 months by Aqara's estimate; a USB-C port gives emergency power.

summary: The Aqara Smart Lock U300 is a lever lock with a fingerprint reader and PIN keypad. It uses Matter over Thread to join Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings, and supports Apple Home Key. Four AA batteries power it, rated up to 10 months. Aqara's pages disagree on whether a hub is required.
caveats: Matter needs a Thread border router; for Apple that means a HomePod mini, HomePod 2nd gen or Apple TV 4K.
The lock binds to one Matter ecosystem at a time; others are added by sharing the pairing code.
Aqara's manual says Matter platforms get only basic functions.
Aqara's pages conflict on whether a hub is required.
